# How TwelveLabs consolidated its fragmented RevOps stack into one GTM engine

![](https://2x.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/case-study-twelvelabs-1024x750.jpg)

## From an underused Clay instance to a connected GTM engine

TwelveLabs, a video understanding AI company, had a lean revenue operations (RevOps) function, an underused Clay instance, and several contractors managing different parts of its technology stack. The fragmented setup created operational overhead and made it difficult to connect lead capture, enrichment, scoring, routing, and outreach.

The Kiln (a 2X company) helped TwelveLabs bring its fragmented RevOps workflows together through a centralized GTM engine. The engagement brought together **nearly a dozen inbound lead sources**, activated personalized outreach across **two platforms**, and replaced multiple RevOps contractor relationships with one trusted partner.

* * *

## The challenge: An underused platform and fragmented RevOps ownership

TwelveLabs had owned Clay for well over a year, but its lean RevOps function had only scratched the surface of the platform’s capabilities.

When VP of Revenue Bobby Moore joined the company, he recognized an opportunity to do more with Clay. The challenge was finding specialists with the technical expertise to take the platform beyond basic enrichment.

Previous consultants had claimed familiarity with Clay but lacked the expertise TwelveLabs needed. Meanwhile, several contractors each managed different parts of the RevOps stack, creating additional coordination work and making it harder to achieve cohesive results.

TwelveLabs needed a partner who could connect its existing systems, improve how leads moved from capture to action, and recommend better technical approaches rather than simply execute requests.

* * *

## The solution: Connect inbound, outreach, and outbound development

The Kiln worked with TwelveLabs across three areas to establish a more connected GTM operation.

##### 1\. Consolidate inbound sources into one engine

The Kiln centralized TwelveLabs’ fragmented inbound sources into a single engine for enrichment, scoring, and routing.

##### The sources included:

- Five or six in-product signals from the TwelveLabs Playground web app
- Trust and security intent leads sourced through Vanta
- Sales inquiry forms in HubSpot
- Marketplace data used for enrichment and outbound
- Additional inbound channels

The centralized system enriched and scored incoming leads, then routed them to the appropriate people using assignment logic.

This gave TwelveLabs a more connected process for managing inbound demand instead of relying on disconnected workflows across its RevOps stack.

##### 2\. Activate personalized outreach across two platforms

The Kiln connected lead enrichment and scoring with personalized outreach across SalesLoft and Instantly.

SalesLoft handled follow-up for enriched and scored inbound leads, while Instantly supported higher-volume outbound activity.

The Kiln also challenged the initial technical approach, recommending Instantly over a more traditional marketing-tool-based setup as a better fit for TwelveLabs’ needs.

##### 3\. Build toward net-new outbound

With the inbound engine running, The Kiln began developing total addressable market (TAM) maps and target account lists.

This work laid the foundation for TwelveLabs to expand beyond warm, opt-in demand and pursue net-new outbound opportunities among high-fit accounts.

The engagement connected the immediate need for stronger inbound operations with the next stage of TwelveLabs’ GTM development.

* * *

## The results: One connected engine and one trusted partner

- **Multiple inbound lead sources consolidated:** Previously fragmented sources were brought together in a centralized engine for enrichment, scoring, and routing.
- **2 outreach platforms activated:** SalesLoft supported personalized inbound follow-up, while Instantly handled higher-volume outbound activity.
- **RevOps contractor relationships consolidated:** TwelveLabs disengaged its previous external RevOps contractors and established The Kiln as its primary partner for this work.
- **A foundation for net-new outbound:** TAM mapping and target account list development began, supporting the move toward outbound targeting of high-fit accounts.
- **Clay established as a central GTM engineering backbone:** TwelveLabs moved beyond basic Clay usage to a more connected system supporting its RevOps processes.

Beyond the technical improvements, TwelveLabs gained a simpler operating relationship. Instead of coordinating multiple contractors, the team could work with one partner that understood how the different parts of its GTM operation fit together.

* * *

## A partner that challenges assumptions and finds better solutions

For TwelveLabs, the value of working with The Kiln extended beyond platform expertise.

Head of Growth Maninder Saini emphasized the difference between contractors who simply follow instructions and specialists who challenge assumptions, propose alternatives, and help determine the best approach.

Throughout the engagement, The Kiln brought that perspective to decisions about platform architecture, workflow design, and the broader GTM operation.
